PullRequest.Title: Reference hover UI improvements addressing post-merge feedback
PullRequest.Body:
This pull request implements several UI improvements based on feedback received after the previous PR was merged. The changes focus on enhancing the hover functionality and ensuring better user experience through various fixes and updates.

### Key Changes
- **Managed Hover Lifecycle**: Improved the dismissal process to cancel asynchronous content and release preview resources.
- **Hover Preservation**: Immediate disposal of rejected hover candidates to prevent leaks.
- **Keyboard Navigation**: Enhanced support for keyboard access in file/image hover actions, allowing for better navigation.
- **Focus Restoration**: Ensured that GitHub hover refreshes restore focus to the appropriate controls.
- **State Checks**: Updated checks to ignore results when the head SHA does not match the current pull request head.
- **Retry Logic**: Implemented retry logic for failed GitHub credential initialization during session references and commits.
- **Regression Tests**: Added comprehensive regression tests to cover all changes, ensuring that the new functionality works as intended.

### Validation
- All changes have passed targeted ESLint checks and unit tests, with a total of **200 passing tests**.
- Visual validation confirmed no unexpected UI changes across **34 affected component fixtures** in both light and dark themes.

This PR is ready for review and further integration into the main branch.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Refreshing an open action-list hover invokes the replacement entry's image content factory as a preservation probe. That factory immediately starts a cancellable fileService.readFile of up to 20 MiB; when the new element is not the one already attached, the pre-fix path discarded it without retaining or disposing its preview handle, so the read and subsequent image allocations could continue for every refresh.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Live session/reference updates while an image row hover is open can leave rejected preview candidates doing unnecessary filesystem/remote-filesystem I/O and retaining their preview resources until completion.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The hover descriptor now exposes disposeContent, and ActionListWidget calls it whenever the factory-created preservation candidate is rejected; the image implementation disposes the candidate and cancels its read immediately.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The base factory at chatDropdownPill.ts:375 creates createChatPillImagePreview on first invocation, whose implementation starts fileService.readFile with a 20 MiB cap. ActionListWidget.updateItems invokes that factory during preserveHover refreshes, and the new RIGHT line 1699 disposes a candidate when preservePanel is false. The added test verifies the rejected replacement token becomes cancelled. The introducing-line blame resolves to the image-preview change 05ffe98d55ba4d22054b6f18366985bd0180d2dc.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: ManagedHoverWidget previously passed its target directly to the rendered HoverWidget, so disposal of that rendered widget did not notify ManagedHoverWidget.onDidHide and therefore did not cancel the CancellationTokenSource owned by an in-flight asynchronous content factory. Such factories include session-summary hover resolution that can activate providers and query session items.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Closing a rendered managed hover through the hover UI could leave its async content computation running after the result was no longer visible, wasting I/O/CPU and retaining associated state until it completed or the managed-hover owner was later disposed.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The rendered hover now receives a wrapper target whose dispose callback invokes ManagedHoverWidget.onDidHide for the current widget, cancelling the in-flight content token as soon as that widget is dismissed.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: HoverWidget.dispose calls its target's dispose method; the base line passed this.target directly, which for HTMLElement-backed managed hovers had no callback to ManagedHoverWidget.onDidHide. The new wrapper calls onDidHide at RIGHT line 100, and the added hoverService test demonstrates the content token transitions to cancelled when the rendered hover is dismissed. ChatRichLink supplies a real async token-aware factory through SessionSummaryHoverService.

Scenarios.Scenario: Refresh an open chat-pill dropdown while an image-reference hover is visible
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A sections observable change synchronously rebuilds dropdown items and ActionListWidget.updateItems probes the focused entry's hover content before updating the list. The image factory starts its read immediately; the visible old preview remains authoritative when the new candidate cannot be preserved.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: fileService.readFile of the referenced image with a 20 MiB size limit
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One candidate read for the single currently expanded row on each relevant dropdown refresh; before this PR, rejected candidates from successive refreshes could overlap until each completed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing preservation probe invoked the replacement factory and abandoned a non-attached element without disposing its preview, allowing the read to continue.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The read is asynchronous and not required for the list refresh itself, but uncancelled candidates consume filesystem/remote-filesystem bandwidth and later image allocation off the visible path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The cost scales with live section-update frequency while one image hover is open and with image size, up to the 20 MiB read cap.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Only one hover can be expanded, but pre-diff rejected reads could accumulate across repeated observable refreshes. The PR disposes each rejected candidate immediately, leaving at most the actual visible preview read.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The descriptor-local preview avoids repeated reads only while the same entry object survives. The thumbnail LRU is consulted after file contents are read, so it does not prevent abandoned candidate reads. The new disposeContent hook cancels rejected candidates.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High; the factory, preservation probe, cancellation handle, and regression test are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Refresh frequency and remote-file latency vary by session, but the abandoned-read mechanism and 20 MiB bound are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: This PR fixes the cleanup regression; it does not introduce a reportable performance issue.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resolve GitHub issue, pull-request, and commit metadata for agent-session pills, including recovery after a credential failure
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Initial pill rendering proceeds with recorded metadata while per-resource observables resolve credentials and refresh live GitHub data asynchronously; enriched labels, checks, and hovers update later. After a credential failure, the next derived-section evaluation retries that failed entry.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve GitHub identity through the credential service (/user)
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Requested by each unique unresolved entry, but concurrent calls share the current credential-generation promise and failures pass through a host/token backoff gate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Each entry attempted credential resolution only once and remained unresolved after failure; the PR permits a later call to retry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the initial pill-render critical path; live metadata waits for it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh a GitHub issue or commit subscription, or the core and checks components of a pull-request subscription
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One subscription per normalized unique issue/PR/commit key; issue and commit perform one refresh, while each PR performs two component refreshes. Retries reach these calls only after credentials recover.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These refreshes already occurred on the first successful attempt; the diff adds the same bounded work only when a previously failed credential attempt is retried.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous and off initial rendering; results trigger observable UI updates.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Network work scales with the number of distinct GitHub references retained by the session, not duplicate URLs, and post-failure retries scale with later section recomputations.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Distinct entries initialize in parallel as before; credential identity work is coalesced globally for the current generation. A PR's core and checks refresh concurrently. No new unbounded parallelism is introduced by repeated get calls while pending.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Resolver maps deduplicate normalized keys and retain successful subscriptions. A DisposableStore is installed before awaiting credentials, preventing duplicate initialization while an attempt is pending. Failure clears only that entry so it can retry; the shared credential service coalesces and backs off failed identity resolution.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High; map keys, pending-state store assignment, retry clearing, credential coalescing, and refresh calls are directly visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Sessions may contain varying numbers of GitHub references and outage duration varies, but normal successful paths are unchanged and outage retries are gated/coalesced.
Scenarios.Verdict: The retry behavior adds bounded recovery work rather than a high-confidence regression; no finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Dismiss or explicitly focus a managed hover
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Hover dismissal disposes HoverWidget, whose target-dispose callback now reaches ManagedHoverWidget.onDidHide and cancels pending content. Explicit show now disposes an existing widget and synchronously schedules one immediate replacement so it can receive focus.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Token-aware asynchronous managed-hover content computation, including session-summary provider activation and lookup
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one computation for a managed hover instance; dismissal now cancels it. An explicit re-show can start one replacement computation per user invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The content computation already started when the hover opened, but rendered-widget disposal did not notify ManagedHoverWidget and could leave it running.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The async computation gates rich hover content but not the underlying editor/chat workflow.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cleanup benefit scales with the number and duration of dismissed async hovers. Replacement cost scales only with explicit user requests to focus an already-visible hover.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The old widget is disposed before replacement, so token-aware content is cancelled before the one replacement starts; there is no accumulating burst from the changed show path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: ManagedHoverWidget does not cache resolved factory output across disposal; owner-specific providers may cache. Cancellation prevents obsolete results from being consumed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for cancellation and single replacement; low expected magnitude for the deliberate recreation cost.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider cost varies, and most direct explicit-show callers use cheap static content; the generic list shortcut can recreate richer content only one target at a time.
Scenarios.Verdict: The dismissal change fixes a cleanup regression. The one-for-one recreation needed for focus does not meet the threshold for a performance finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Refresh live pull-request hover contents while a footer control has focus
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A pull-request snapshot change rebuilds section entries; if the dropdown and hover are open, the preservation probe creates fresh hover DOM, replaces the cached root's children, and restores focus to the corresponding new control before list update completes.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Synchronous DOM work is limited to the single expanded hover and scales with that hover's small fixed set of controls, not all session references.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All DOM replacement and focus work is synchronous on the UI thread, once per relevant snapshot update for the one open hover.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Hover roots are cached per normalized link and removed when metadata no longer retains the link; child content is refreshed in place.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High; the open-hover-only call path and cache cardinality are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Snapshot update rates vary, but the added work is a single active-element lookup, short tabbable-element scan, and focus operation after DOM replacement that already occurred.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; the added synchronous work is bounded to one visible hover and preserves focus during an existing refresh.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 15 changed files and all diff pages. No diff-introduced performance finding met the required confidence and impact threshold. Recorded two concrete cleanup-lifecycle regression fixes: cancellation/disposal of rejected image-preview candidates and cancellation of async managed-hover content when the rendered widget is dismissed.
